/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Action_Bi:
TITLE: Action Biker, Tune #1
 ARTIST: Rob Hubbard
COMMENT: "This is a remix from Rob Hubbard's Action Biker main theme (tune #1)
         from the year 1985! (C) Mastertronic. Listen to the original and hear
         the difference! I first typed over the notes (bass + lead) from a Music
         Assembler example tune. Not using the ugly percussion track. The
         chords are typed over from a Midi file called Biker. (Lazy me eh?!).
         Maybe this will not be necessary in future because there is a Midi to
         Mod program and buddy Roland Hermans has made a Mod to Sid program.
         I'm not quite happy with this tune because of the weak 2 notes
         arpeggio part (from 1:14 to 1:50). I made the volume of this arpeggio
         part a bit softer so it becomes a bit less annoying. Maybe I will
         improve this tune sometime. Same presets used as in Rolfie Title
         Remix. Typing over the notes took some amount of time (I always work
         slowly!). I used too many sequences in the 2nd track (it can only
         handle 128). So Roland Hermans "packed" several sequences into only a
         few so the player can handle them. This is the 2nd tune for mainly
         Polish based group Axelerate. Tune is played at CIA 1 Timer A (PAL)
         because we wanted another speed than a normal one. Tune has nice
         ending, don't you agree? Hope you like it!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Advanced_:
COMMENT: "I went into this project wanting to write a "classic" SID that people
         want to listen to frequently perhaps even like a good 80s game SID.
         Soon I noticed I had too few good ideas myself so I used some
         "borrowed" music in this one in true Rob Hubbard style (he also covered
         a lot as you know). So some of other composer's music was the basis of
         some tunes varied with own ideas and combinations of these 2. Of course
         Roland Hermans (Neo) helped me with the technical bits." (JW)
(#1)
   NAME: Intro Tune
COMMENT: "The short intro jingle still went some work in it being quite complex.
         The end sounds particularly well with that kick sound attached to the
         bass." (JW)
(#2)
   NAME: The War Begins
  TITLE: Spybreak! [from Decksandrumsandrockandroll] (1:16-2:33)
 ARTIST: Propellerheads
COMMENT: "As you can hear in The War Begins I like the Matt Gray style. It's
         simple to do and still sounds great. The combination with the Matrix
         tune works well I think. Also I listened to a lot of hard rock/heavy
         metal music to get inspired. A lot of what Matt Gray did can be
         identified with this style. Using double bass plus MG drums is a good
         combination plus after that a ring modulation lead sounds nice." (JW)
(#3)
   NAME: Massive Attack
COMMENT: "Massive Attack begins with 2 tracks shooting SFX from the game
         Dominator. Then a Star Wars alike film tune. The piece after that the
         Jon Dunn's Robocop lead instrument fits and sounds so well! Some funny
         kicks and snares in different volumes. The last piece is very short 'n
         simple and still sounds good. Only a few sequences used. About 4 if I
         remember well." (JW)
(#4)
   NAME: Arduous Battle
COMMENT: "Arduous Battle is completely done by me. In a lot of places the bass
         notes are harder on the beat. In this I made a 64 version of a tune I
         composed on the Amiga with Protracker which was called Freedom. What I
         really like about this tune is the end part which was also first
         composed on the Amiga." (JW)
(#5)
   NAME: The Tragic One
COMMENT: "Sniff sniff! A very melancholic beginning. Then some sort of Philip
         Glass stuff which ends with an attempt to do something similar to
         Hubbard's Knucklebusters tune #2 ending." (JW)
(#6)
   NAME: Final Conquest
  TITLE: Captain Future [from cartoon series Captain Future] (2:59-5:33)
 ARTIST: Christian Bruhn
COMMENT: "Another fine tune beginning to get your attention immediately! A bit
         filmesque start. Then a very nice Captain Future cover with some
         fantastic stretched arpeggios in it. The break in this part is my
         friend Roland's favourite (You know him from the PSID64 program). And
         the last part is composed by myself using some Galway Rambo tune #5
         instruments which I made a bit harder volume wise. Oh yes the
         instrument of the arpeggios is an enhanced version of Jason Brooke's
         Bismarck arp. preset." (JW)
(#7)
   NAME: Space Explorer
COMMENT: "Space Explorer has a very mysterious intro. As you can hear Philip
         Glass is one of my favourite composers. Jam jam! Sounds very nice! The
         ending uses a technique I use whenever it suits: divide the notes over
         2 tracks and play them slightly over eachother. Always sounds very
         good!" (JW)
(#8)
   NAME: Worm Hole in 1
COMMENT: "I'm very pleased with the first part of this one. Cool and agressive!
         Than Matt Gray meets Rob Hubbard! Technically one of the best I've
         written so far. Wooo! Wicked part from 2:02! Speed change in music
         player is handy! Bit boring end of 1st part. I got tired of writing for
         ASB. End part has it's moments. Robocop lead keeps ruling!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/All_B_ear:
(#1)
  TITLE: Passacaglia
 ARTIST: <?>
COMMENT: "A partial cover of a music which was one of the demo tunes in the
         Amiga music program Deluxe Music Construction Set. Bass resembles a
         bit the first part of House of the Rising Sun by The Animals when the
         singing starts. Used as jiffy sound on my 1st music colly!" (JW)
(#2)
  TITLE: Yogi Bear Song
 ARTIST: Hoyt Stoddard Curtin (music), William Hanna & Joseph Barbera (lyrics)
COMMENT: "From the animated TV series "Yogi Bear" composed in 1960. This was
         harder to convert than I expected. I asked some acquaintances to help
         me out but they couldn't. So I did it myself and there are no off key
         notes in this! Presets are from Parasol Stars tunes. An mp3 was the
         example for this. Used as Title tune of my 1st music colly!" (JW)

COMMENT: "Own composed in true JW style! To get going making midi files I'm
         making a midi cover of this. I'd better make those chords notes
         slower (I want to go towards making music for a band). Instead of
         using slides I used Dane's technique (in Whistle song): a length 1
         note for some lead notes. Used as Turn disk music in my 1st music
         colly." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Arabian_N:
COMMENT: "Demo containing this tune had a nice "gadget" enclosed. The drive led
         reacted on 1 of the tracks. (Ofcourse coded by Roland Hermans). I only
         just came up with the title of this song after Roland changed
         something in the presets (instruments) which gave it an Arabian touch.
         Ok I think. Composed on piano." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Archimede:
TITLE: The Raiders March [from all the Indiana Jones movies]
 ARTIST: John Williams
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/As_de_ste:
TITLE: As de sterre dao baove straole
 ARTIST: Arthur "Thuur" Luxembourg (music), Frans Boermans (lyrics)
COMMENT: "The demo in which this sound was spread contained the full lyrics of
         the song written in South Dutch dialect. This tune consists of a
         double lead to get a sort of echo effect. The reason why I made this
         song: In the south of Holland we celibrate Carnival each year around
         the end of February and because I live in a provence of Southern
         Holland called Limburg I decided to make one of the best Carnival
         songs on the C64! During Carnival everyone dresses up in some strange
         costume and goes into pubs to party and of course drink a lot of beer.
         The title of the song translated into English is: When the stars are
         shining up there. Written in waltz tempo. Hope you like it." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Beast_III:
TITLE: press fire [from the Amiga game Shadow of the Beast III]
 ARTIST: Tim Wright
COMMENT: "Of course I had to squeeze the Amiga 4 tracks in to C64's 3. But the
         tune uses 2 tracks for the part which isn't the lead or bass. How do
         you call that part anyway? (backing?) While going through old Amiga
         500 games with buddy Roland (we were looking through because we are
         planning a C64 demo consisting converted Amiga pics in FLI-Interlace)
         we stumbled upon this tune. I like it very much so I tried if I could
         rip it with my Datel Electronics' Amiga Action Replay MK III. I froze
         the game and typed in tracker. And golly yes! The cartridge found the
         tune and I saved it to disc and loaded it in my Protracker soundtool.
         Together with Roland I converted it. (He works much quicker than me).
         We are planning to do more conversions. After this conversion Roland
         made a program to convert from MOD to SID, right into my player as
         I said in Action Biker Remix STIL text. But now it even converts
         arpeggios! The presets are: bass from Psycho Pigs UXB. Flute resembles
         Amiga lead sample instrument but has a little waveform 41 tick at
         the beginning and is made by Roland. Other preset is from Henning
         Rokling's Henning_Rokling-02.sid which is used in demo Wild At Heart.
         We first made an arpeggio sound consisting of two different c notes
         but it didn't work out well. In beginning of the tune you can hear a
         build up of decay and sustain in this preset. To get this effect we
         had to make 4 presets just changing the decay and sustain from 2 to 8.
         The wave on effects on bass and Rokling preset make it sound ok on
         C64. Often this effect is used to substitute normal hi hat sounds.
         This ditty is one of my favourite tunes!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Because_I:
TITLE: Because I Got High
 ARTIST: Afroman
COMMENT: "Before I saw the movie Jay & Silent Bob Strike back (this
         zax was the end music of the hilarious film) I wanted to
         make a cover of this afrolicious tune! It's probably the
         only tune they made which is cool. This C64 version is
         a bit faster, probably in an other key and is fast composed.
         The arpeggio lead was taken from my Space Harrier Remix.
         Respect!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Blackadde:
TITLE: Blackadder [from the TV series]
 ARTIST: Howard Goodall
COMMENT: "The one that drove JW insane was Blackadder Theme. I was looking and
         looking for bass notes but never found any that sounded good! So I
         decided to let them out and use 2 voices for the lead. The idea to
         make this mini tune was that I coincidentally found a nice midi file
         on the net from which I only used the background. Preset of this is
         taken from Demon's Aural Manouvers II. I listened to the original TV
         theme on the BBC and was surprised to find out that I liked this
         version more than the original!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Bladerunn:
TITLE: Blade Runner (End Titles) [from the movie]
 ARTIST: Vangelis
COMMENT: "This zax covers the techno version by Tyrell Bros. The kick and bass
         sound much better on a real C64. Finding the fast notes needed some
         time until I found out the notes were also in the chords. Kick sound
         was taken from a tune by Sad rest done by me and Roland. A midi tune

TITLE: Duncan [from Pubs, Trucks and Plains]
 ARTIST: Slim Dusty
COMMENT: "Unkle K asked me to cover this tune for Reset #05 Intro so I made a quick
         rendition. I must say I like this one the most of all Dusty's tracks." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Especiall:
TITLE: Stille Nacht! Heilige Nacht!
 ARTIST: Joseph Mohr (lyrics), Franz Xaver Gruber (music)
COMMENT: "This little zax was hence the name especially made for a man I know
         from my home village who collects all existing versions of the Silent
         Night tune. This tune was used in a Covenant demo for the X-mas
         competition 2003." (JW)
COMMENT: "Game was made (like Tough Guys) by Ramon (BB) van de Laar. And it's
         about a forester who has to paint the brown leaves green again
         avoiding EVIL forest animals. It was a real pain in the ass to play
         but was awarded as one of the best games in '92.
         My pally Roland Hermans (ex-Einstein/RGJ/Smidas from ATG (Actual
         Trading Generation) always helped me with the technical bits of C64
         music like players and presets etc. Some presets throughout this game
         music are from Johannes Bjerregaard's Flimbo's Quest. There's one I
         used as lead, bass and as arpeggio (chords)." (JW)
(#1)
COMMENT: "This is the congratulations tune consisting a Follin like melody row
         of fast notes made by Roland Hermans. The filter lead in the
         beginning is from Jeroen Tel's Myth tune #3. As you can hear I very
         much like to leave the bass away at the end of zaxes to get a nice
         "echo" effect." (JW)
(#2)
COMMENT: "This level tune #1, a 2-voice zax made in a simple march tempo. The
         other track was used as sound-fx track. I thought about putting in a
         3rd optional drum track or extra lead track but this was thought to be
         not necessary." (JW)
(#3)
COMMENT: "This is the second level zax, also 2-voiced. Bit more cheerful than
         the 1st level zax. Bits of the melody popped into my mind when I was
         cycling home from school." (JW)
(#4)
  TITLE: Canon in D major
 ARTIST: Johann Pachelbel
COMMENT: "I used a Tim Follin bass from Psycho Pigs UXB tune #1. The harmonica
         is from Follin's Black Lamp, Tune #1." (JW)
(#5)
COMMENT: "This is the game over tune. First made in Dutch USA team's Music
         Assembler. I made this tune not knowing what it would become. But it
         fits its purpose very nicely I think." (JW)
(#6)
COMMENT: "This is the high score tune. Before Forester this sound was published
         (slightly different from this one) as "Ode to Junior". Junior was a
         cat that we had at my elderly home. Was, because he's now in cat's
         heaven. Tune was made in a period I didn't know how to make use of
         arpeggio's (chord substitutes). It's still ok, I guess." (JW)
(#7)
COMMENT: "This is the bonus level tune. It's made a bit faster than the level
         tunes to get that hectic feel. Funny is the extreme fast part starting
         from (1:41) which may make the game even more difficult to play if you
         let yourself be influenced by the sound." (JW)
(#8)
  TITLE: Kwik Snax, Tune #6
 ARTIST: Robert Westgate
COMMENT: "This is the end of level zax. Without knowing I somewhat copied tune
         #6 from Codemasters' Kwik Snax. I used 2 tracks for the lead to get
         that sort of echo stuff in." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Gameboy_T:
TITLE: High Score [from the Game Boy game Tetris]
 ARTIST: Hirokazu Tanaka (Hip)
COMMENT: "This is 1 of my 2 all time Game Boy favorites, the 1st is of course
         Super Mario Land. This zax has the same structure as Blackadder Theme
         but the lead in Blackadder is more fluty. The midi tune I found on the
         net had some faults in it. But they were soon ironed out by me." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Glasswork:
TITLE: Opening/Closing [from Glassworks]
 ARTIST: Philip Glass
COMMENT: "This is my 2nd Glass cover and there will follow more. This is
         converted from a midi file I found on the net. All presets are the
         same but the bass preset is a bit softer. This preset is from
         Jonathan Dunn's Robocop. Very nice pulse thingy in it. The lead from
         1:55 is done by me." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Gray_Runn:
TITLE: Blade Runner (End Titles) [from the movie]
 ARTIST: Vangelis
COMMENT: "This zax is a Matt Gray alike version of Bladerunner end
         titles, hence the name. It was used in one of JSL's entries
         for the gfx competition on Vision 2003. I thought a nice
         picture needs a nice sound. Pity the music was not played
         during the gfx compo. This was changed in comparison with
         last year's party. Bass preset is from a Boogaloo sound,
         Matt Gray drums were surprisingly not taken from one of
         his sounds but from a Fanta tune, lead done by Roland. First
         use of ring modulation of this kind in a tune by me!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Gryzor_Ti:
TITLE: Sandinista (Ending) [from the arcade game Contra]
 ARTIST: Kazuki Muraoka
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Honey_Bee:
(#3)
  TITLE: Tiroler Holzhacker Buab'n (op. 356)
 ARTIST: Joseph Franz Wagner
COMMENT: "First part was written for Curly Squirrel game which never saw the
         light of day." (JW)
TITLE: Infinity [from Infinity]
 ARTIST: Guru Josh
COMMENT: "If I had the knowledge I now have when I made this piece I certainly
         would have put in some chords and combined the drums and bass in one
         track like Moz(IC)Art did (the best version on the C64). Reyn
         Ouwehand's version also has its moments. Though I think my version has
         the most resembling saxophone sound on this compy." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Knight_n_:
TITLE: Knight'n'Grail, Tune #9
 ARTIST: Hans Axelsson
COMMENT: Covers /MUSICIANS/T/The_Dungeon_Master/Knight_n_Grail.sid, Tune #9.
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Koyaanisq:
TITLE: Koyaanisqatsi [from the movie]
 ARTIST: Philip Glass
COMMENT: "Glass' own style is called "minimalistic music". I got the music on
         tape from pally Paultje (M0k) Kessels, I thought it was brill and
         converted it into Dutch USA team's Music Assembler. Bass is nice,
         original MA drums are awful." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Kung_Fu_F:
TITLE: Kung Fu Fighting [from Kung Fu Fighting]
 ARTIST: Carl Douglas
COMMENT: "This is what you get when you have to make a tune on a party (Vision
         2002) in a hurry without a keyboard! Exile/Anubis made a pic of a toy
         hamster singing this song. (one of the compo prizes). That's why I
         made this. I changed the text which is in the beginning of this tune
         at $1000 into: please don't rip this music etc. But yeah! those guys
         of the HVSC crew want every SID ever made in the HVSC. So that's why
         it's in here! Oh sigh!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Lady_Hear:
TITLE: Lady
 ARTIST: Modjo
COMMENT: "Modjo made a cover of Chic's Soup For One from 1982. Composers were
         Bernard Edwards and Nile Rodgers. Modjo's version is much faster.
         Something which you see more lately in covers. This music was made for
         D-Pac, he made a textro to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the 64!
         It was released on 19th of October 2002 at the special edition of the
         Dutch HCC computer show. As you can hear this sound uses a 2 tracks
         snare which was taken from Tim Follin's Qix. Hope U like it!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Linko.sid:
COMMENT: "This game was a conversion of a popular word game on tv in Holland
         and even was sometime in Germany on the telly in which you get one
         letter of the 5 or 6 and have to guess which word it is, roughly said.
         It's been on the Dutch telly for years and years now, and still is
         very popular. Game was coded by pally Roland Hermans. And the music
         consists of several covers." (JW)
(#1)
  TITLE: Ritmo de la Noche
 ARTIST: Mystic
COMMENT: "This is the title theme and means in English: Rhythm of the night.
         Mystic's version was based on: I go to Rio from Peter Allen and Ritmo
         de la Noche by Chocolate. It contains 5 tracks: 3 normal and 2
         separate digi tracks consisting of a drum track and some several
         chords track. Was first made with Protracker on my old and trusty
         Amiga 500." (JW)
(#2)
COMMENT: "The row of notes (not the bass or lead) is borrowed from a music I
         heard in the heroic cartoon series Prince Valiant and is used as high
         score music. It consists again a bass from Tim Follin's Psycho Pigs
         UXB tune #1. Lead is again of Jeroen Tel's Myth tune #3 this time
         without filter. Of course the old trick is used to divide the notes
         over 2 tracks." (JW)
(#3)
  TITLE: I Promised Myself [from Move Until We Fly] (1:01-1:47)
 ARTIST: Nick Kamen
COMMENT: "This is the ingame music and consists of 3 parts: The first I wrote
         myself, and the 3rd is also self made, hear that super fast bass!
         The second part is a cover, mentioned above." (JW)
(#4)
  TITLE: Hazard
 ARTIST: Richard Marx
COMMENT: "This is the game over tune. Also first use of slide effects
         (portamento) in my music to give that extra edge." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Lullaby.s:
COMMENT: "Called sleeping song because Roland thought it was a song from which
         you get very sleepy. The chords are taken from the beginning of the
         music of a Dutch USA team demo called Nemesis, I made use of some
         sawtooth presets to get that Galway feel. Bassline is simply using a C
         note and the C note an octave higher. Made in Music Assembler which
         was shortened by pally Roland Hermans, so it only occupies memory from
         $1000-$12EF on the C64 which is 3 blocks (less than 1 K!). Neil
         Baldwin's Music Demo Number One was an example for me, using 2 tracks
         for lead when the bass is suspended. The nicest thing of the C64 SID
         chip is that you can create a warm analogue sound." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/MK_II.sid:
COMMENT: "Was used in the Spanish SF adventure MK II. Music is played when the
         awesome intro pic is shown which makes it sound even better! Again the
         Matt Gray minimalistic style was used but I added some of my own ideas
         as well as you can hear." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Masterpie:
COMMENT: "An experimental piece. This was the least bad version. Composed on
         piano and by voice." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Merlins_D:
TITLE: titlemusic v2 [from the Amiga game Double Dragon III] (2:48-3:57)
 ARTIST: Andrew Barnabas (Night-Shade)
COMMENT: "This is my Mekka Symposium 2001 SID competition entry. It finished
         11th from the 29 and got 32 votes. Too bad there is no independent
         jury on the Mekka party so if you know a lot of people who will vote
         for you, you will finish 1st. The first part (from 0:00 to 0:45) was
         made back in '92. The rest was made in 2 weeks in 2001. At the party
         SIDs are played up to 4 minutes. So I had to stop at the end of the
         4th minute. Since this msx contains a sample beat it must be played on
         an old SID, as was done on the party. You had to mention on the entry
         sheet which SID they had to use. Too bad the music was played too soft
         on the party (held during Easter). The zax might be a bit too
         long-winded. The DD III part was converted from an Amiga MOD" (JW)
         The Double Dragon III music is better known by its real name of Water
         II and was one of the tracks on Andrew Barnabas' CD.

TITLE: Parasol Stars High Score [from the PC Engine game]
 ARTIST: Turbo Mira, Yasuko

TITLE: Parasol Stars ingame [from the PC Engine game]
 ARTIST: Turbo Mira, Yasuko
COMMENT: "This is a conversion of an Amiga Octamed file I found on the net. It
         was my entry for the Vision party 2001. It was the best music but
         since there were not enough entries, all entries were put into 1
         competition. It finished 4th. All presets were done by buddy Roland
         Hermans which very much sound like the Amiga ones. Great job! I always
         wanted to convert this tune and fortunately I found the Med files
         which saved me from very much work. 11 presets were used among a
         filter bass preset. I really like this tune! Anyone also wants to make
         a complete game conversion?" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Remember_:
TITLE: No Holly for Miss Quinn [from Shepherd Moons]
 ARTIST: Enya
COMMENT: "I started working on this tune before an update came out with the
         tune in it done by Harti. But his version was much slower, divided
         the background notes over 2 tracks and left out a piece of the
         original. It sounded nice but without wanting to sound arrogant I like
         my version better! All presets done by Roland! It finished 3rd on the
         Vision 2003 music compo which made me win 2 C64 related cds!" (JW)

/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Robbels.s:
COMMENT: "Composed on piano at the beginning of the 90s. So the SID came much
         later. Was used in the music colly 10 Years HVSC. I made a pc version
         of it for a children's music project (Knorrie On The Farm translated)
         which sounds much better because you can have as many tracks as you
         want and you can use instruments that sound like real ones (VSTi's).
         But I think the SID also has its charm!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Robin_Hoo:
TITLE: The Adventures of Robin Hood intro [from the Amiga game]
 ARTIST: Richard Joseph
COMMENT: "This is a conversion of one of my favourite Amiga tunes. Again I had
         to squeeze the 4 tracks into 3. So I had to leave out some things but
         you don't really miss them. Roland did a fine job with the
         instruments. Especially the lead instrument starting from 0:24 is
         great! This tune was used in the Richard Joseph Tribute Demo in the
         intro and in the music menu as well." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Robocod_i:
TITLE: James Pond II - RoboCod (toys) [from the Amiga game]
 ARTIST: Richard Joseph
COMMENT: "I went through several RJ tunes to make a SID cover for the Richard
         Joseph Tribute Demo. I was very attracted by the 'James Pond II -
         Codename RoboCod' Amiga tunes. I saw the best tune catlots a.k.a.
         ingame 1 was already covered in the C64 version of the game so I chose
         the 'toys' tune which is also great. Good thing the original is also
         in 3 tracks so I didn't have to leave anything out. Again some nice
         instruments by Roland!" (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Rolfie_Ti:
COMMENT: "This is a remix of the title theme I made for a children's cd rom I
         am making together with some pallies of mine. The cd rom is called
         "Rolfie Op Wereldreis" which is translated: "Rolfie On A World Trip"
         and is about a cat which travels around the world visiting 10
         countries from which England and America are divided into 2 pages. So
         in total there are 12 different country drawings, a title page, a
         credits page and and end page. With every page there comes an
         appropriate, spheric music plus lyrics about what can be seen in the
         drawings. All the sight seeing objects can be seen in a picture of
         each country. For instance in Egypt you can see: some pyramids, a
         sphinx, the Nile, a palm tree, some background items and Rolfie the
         cat on a camel. When you click on an object it starts to animate and a
         WAV-file begins to play making e.g. a camel sound and telling a story
         about e.g. a camel. This title tune is apart from the melody altered
         heavily to let it sound ok on the C64. This is the first tune I made
         since 1992 which was spread, so you can call it a sort of test tune.
         And this is also the first tune made for mainly Poland based group
         Axelerate which has died in the beginning of 2001. All presets are the
         same as in Linko music except before every bass sound (from 0:15),
         there is a kick drum sound added. Idea for 3 track chords in beginning
         is from Reyn Ouwehand's Deadlock (brilliant title tune). Wind sound
         was added, as always if something needs to be added, it was done by
         pally Roland 'Neo' Hermans. Hope U like it!" (JW)

/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Star_Wars:
TITLE: Main Title [from all the Star Wars movies]

         del Soft (translated: The Software Donkeys!) which was the gfx colly
         "Robot Nation". They needed a SF tune and I immediately thought of
         this tune. I think this is one of the best tunes John Williams did.
         I must say I also like the movies. Remarkable is that a lot of John's
         music is written in mainly C. Maybe that's the key to his success!
         This SID is an ok rendition I guess!" (JW)

         lead might be a bit different because of those special echo thingies

/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Tough_Guy:

         "Bonzobrok" v.d. Laar. I got some help from Charles Deenen (ex-Maniacs
         of Noise). Before he went to the States he used to live on cycling
         distance of my domicile in the Southern part of Holland." (JW)
(#1)

         also I copied a cd from him with Japanese music (forgot the name)
         which was the basis for the last part of the title theme, from 1:27,
         and the complete level zax." (JW)
(#2)

         Hubbard's IK+ and also Rob's tune was an example for me to get a bit
         agressive level sound." (JW)
(#3)
  TITLE: Chambers of Shaolin (title) [from the Amiga game]
 ARTIST: Jochen Hippel (Mad Max)
COMMENT: "The melody was found using the black keys on my keyboard which always
         bring an oriental melody. Also we (I always cooperate with Roland
         Hermans, who is a good programmer) got some tips from Charles how to
         get an oriental sound by making appropiate presets (instruments) using
         arpeggio's and flute sounds. As you can hear much transpose is used in
         all songs. This is the end of game tune." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Truman_Sl:
TITLE: Truman Sleeps [from the movie]
 ARTIST: Philip Glass
COMMENT: "The 3rd Glass cover partially covered from a midi file. It didn't
         work out as well as I had expected but however it is a bit short it's
         ok I guess. It's the eight tune used in Arachnophobia mag #24 which
         makes that mag a true Yogibear special! What I learned from this tune
         is that the $11 wave form (in this case flute sound) is a good choice
         to use for the 2nd lead voice which is of course less dominant than
         the 1st. Thanx again to Neo for helping with the presets but in the
         future I hope I can do them myself as I'm learning how my music player
         and the SID chip works." (JW)
/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Turrican_:
TITLE: Freedom [from the Amiga game Turrican II]
 ARTIST: Chris Hülsbeck
COMMENT: "Tune was used in ArachnoPhobia#29. It's another midi cover.
         Begin preset again from Fame's X-Out music. Using this sounds a lot
         better than the arpeggios as background. Cool tune huh!
         It sounds best with a bass booster!" (JW)

TITLE: The Great Bath (level 2-1) [from the Amiga game Turrican II]
 ARTIST: Chris Hülsbeck
COMMENT: "This is one of the fastest conversions I ever done and still I really
         like it! Yes, a midi file was the original. A lot of dividing notes
         over 2 tracks technique was used, which always sounds good! This was
         my Vision 2002 party entry, it finished 10th in the mixed compo. Cool
         tune huh!" (JW)

TITLE: Air Combat (level 3) [from the Amiga game Turrican III]
 ARTIST: Chris Hülsbeck
COMMENT: "Another MIDI file conversion taken from the Video Game Music Archive
         (www.vgmusic.com). It was first intended to be a high score music for
         a shoot'em up from Protovision, but they didn't want covers in their
         games. Roland and I first put the filter on the arpeggios like Robocop
         title but in most cases it is best to put it on the bass like we did
         in this tune. I think this is one of the best basslines I ever heard.
         It's pretty complex! Chris is/was probably the best German computer
         zax composer ever. I think! The arpeggios are not chords they consist
         of 2 notes. Lead is from Dunn's Robocop title, rest by Roland. Hope U
         like it!" (JW)

TITLE: Interlevel [from the Amiga game Turrican II]
 ARTIST: Chris Hülsbeck
COMMENT: "Big User of Protovision needed a quick, o.k. tune for his Vision 2002
         party entry called Mega Turrican (GFX). And that's what I did. That
         background preset thingie was taken from X-Out, which was used there
         as lead. Again a midi file was the basis for this one. From 0:50 an
         extra effect was added courtesy Roland. Thanx! I must say it sounded
         really cool on the party with that thumping bass! As you can hear the
         drums were linked to the bass." (JW)

 ARTIST: Marnix van St. Aldegonde (lyrics), Valerius (music)
COMMENT: It is based on an old French soldiers tune.

/MUSICIANS/W/Wijnhoven_Joachim/Yogis_Fre:
TITLE: La Marseillaise (French National Anthem)
 ARTIST: Claude Joseph Rouget de Lisle
